title.en: Encrypting a file you read from the middle: cipher modes (R1 · 2)
title.zh: 从中间读的加密文件：密码的工作模式（复1 · 2）

description.en: What a block cipher does to a file, why plain ECB leaks patterns, why chained modes make random access hard, how counter mode makes every block independent, and the one rule counter mode must never break.
description.zh: 分组密码怎样处理一个文件，为什么直接用 ECB 会泄露规律，为什么链式模式让随机访问变难，计数器模式怎样让每一块各自独立，以及计数器模式绝不能破的那条规矩。

name.zh: 对称密钥算法：DES 与 AES (symmetric-key algorithms, DES, AES)

name.en: Block cipher modes: ECB, CBC, CFB, stream cipher and counter modes
name.zh: 分组密码的工作模式：ECB、CBC、CFB、流密码与计数器 (cipher modes)
密钥流重用攻击 (keystream reuse attack)

description.en: Choosing ECB for random access without seeing that it reveals repeated blocks
description.zh: 为了随机访问选 ECB，却没看到它会暴露重复的块

title.zh: 复习课 (1) · 样题 2（模拟卷第 16 题）

paras.en: An encrypted file needs to be accessed in non-sequential order. Which cipher mode is best suited to encrypting this file, and briefly explain why.
paras.zh: 一个加密文件需要按非顺序的方式访问。哪种密码工作模式最适合加密这个文件？简要解释原因。

items.en: **An encrypted file**: a file on disk, encrypted with a symmetric block cipher such as AES (the same key encrypts and decrypts).
items.zh: **加密文件**：磁盘上的一个文件，用 AES 这类对称分组密码加密（加密和解密用同一个密钥）。

items.en: **Accessed in non-sequential order**: random access. A database file, or a video in which you jump to minute 40: you want block 1000 without going through blocks 1 to 999, and perhaps you want to change it and write it back.
items.zh: **按非顺序访问**：随机访问。比如一个数据库文件，或者一段视频你想直接跳到第 40 分钟：你要第 1000 块，而不想从第 1 块走到第 999 块，也许还要改了它再写回去。

items.en: **Cipher mode**: the rule for applying a block cipher to a long run of blocks. The course names five: electronic code book, cipher block chaining, cipher feedback, stream cipher and counter mode.
items.zh: **密码工作模式**（cipher mode）：把分组密码用在一长串块上的规则。课上讲了五种：电子密码本、密码块链接、密码反馈、流密码和计数器模式。

text.en: The ideas: what the plainest mode does and why it is not enough; why chaining blocks together, the usual fix, gets in the way of random access; and how counter mode avoids both problems.
text.zh: 需要的想法：最朴素的模式怎么做、为什么不够；通常的补救办法——把块串起来——为什么妨碍了随机访问；以及计数器模式怎样同时避开这两个问题。

title.en: A block cipher, and the trouble with using it plainly
title.zh: 分组密码，以及直接用它的毛病

text.en: A block cipher encrypts one fixed-size block at a time: 64 bits for DES, 128 bits for AES. With key $K$, it turns a plaintext block $P$ into a ciphertext block $C = E_K(P)$, and $D_K(C) = P$ turns it back. A file is many blocks, $P_1, P_2, P_3, \dots$
text.zh: 分组密码一次加密一个固定大小的块：DES 是 64 位，AES 是 128 位。用密钥 $K$，它把明文块 $P$ 变成密文块 $C = E_K(P)$，$D_K(C) = P$ 再把它变回来。一个文件就是很多块：$P_1, P_2, P_3, \dots$

text.en: The plainest way is **electronic code book (ECB)** mode: encrypt each block on its own, $C_i = E_K(P_i)$. Random access is easy, since block 1000 is just $E_K(P_{1000})$. But the same plaintext block always gives the same ciphertext block. Files are full of repeats (headers, blank areas, records with the same fields), so an eavesdropper sees where the repeats are, and can even swap or replay blocks without knowing the key. The course's slide: the same text leads to the same ciphertext, unless something else is done.
text.zh: 最朴素的方式是**电子密码本**（ECB）模式：每块单独加密，$C_i = E_K(P_i)$。随机访问很容易，第 1000 块就是 $E_K(P_{1000})$。但同样的明文块总是变成同样的密文块。文件里到处是重复（文件头、空白区域、字段相同的记录），窃听者能看出哪里重复，甚至不知道密钥也能调换或重放某些块。课件的说法：同样的文本得到同样的密文，除非另想办法。

title.en: Chained modes: each block depends on the one before
title.zh: 链式模式：每块都依赖前一块

text.en: **Cipher block chaining (CBC)**: before encrypting a block, XOR it with the previous ciphertext block; the first block is XORed with a random **initialisation vector** (IV): $C_i = E_K(P_i \oplus C_{i-1})$. Identical plaintext blocks now give different ciphertext.
text.zh: **密码块链接**（CBC）：加密一个块之前，先把它和前一个密文块做异或；第一块和一个随机的**初始化向量**（IV）异或：$C_i = E_K(P_i \oplus C_{i-1})$。这样一来，相同的明文块会得到不同的密文。

text.en: **Cipher feedback (CFB)** works a byte at a time, which suits data produced a byte at a time, such as keystrokes. A register holding the last 8 bytes of ciphertext is encrypted, and one byte of the result is XORed with the next plaintext byte. So each byte depends on the 8 ciphertext bytes before it (and a single wrong bit in the ciphertext spoils 9 bytes of the decrypted text).
text.zh: **密码反馈**（CFB）一次处理一个字节，适合一个字节一个字节产生的数据，比如击键。一个存着最近 8 个密文字节的寄存器被加密，结果中的一个字节和下一个明文字节异或。所以每个字节都依赖它前面的 8 个密文字节（密文里错一位，解密出来就会坏掉 9 个字节）。

alt.en: Top, CBC: five blocks; each ciphertext block feeds the XOR of the next block; block 4 and the arrow into it from C3 are highlighted, and block 5 is dashed. Bottom, counter mode: five independent columns, IV+i encrypted and XORed with P_i to give C_i; only block 4 is highlighted.
alt.zh: 上，CBC：五个块；每个密文块都送进下一块的异或；第 4 块以及从 C3 进来的箭头被标出，第 5 块是虚线。下，计数器模式：五列互不相关，IV+i 加密后与 P_i 异或得到 C_i；只有第 4 块被标出。

caption.en: Top: in CBC, block 4 needs $C_3$, and its own $C_4$ feeds block 5, so changing block 4 changes every block after it. Bottom: in counter mode, block 4 needs only the key, the IV and its own number.
caption.zh: 上：CBC 里，第 4 块需要 $C_3$，它自己的 $C_4$ 又送进第 5 块，所以改动第 4 块，后面的每一块都跟着变。下：计数器模式里，第 4 块只需要密钥、IV 和它自己的编号。

text.en: For random access, this chaining gets in the way. To decrypt a block in the middle, you must also fetch the ciphertext before it (for CFB, the 8 preceding bytes). And to change a block in the middle, you would have to re-encrypt everything after it, because each block feeds the next.
text.zh: 对随机访问来说，这种链接碍事了。要解密中间的一块，得把它前面的密文也取来（CFB 是前面 8 个字节）。要改中间的一块，就得把它后面的全部重新加密，因为每一块都喂给下一块。

title.en: Stream cipher mode and counter mode
title.zh: 流密码模式和计数器模式

text.en: A different idea: do not run the data through the cipher at all. Encrypt something else to make a **keystream**, and XOR the keystream with the data. XOR with the same keystream again undoes it, so decryption is the same operation as encryption.
text.zh: 换个思路：根本不让数据过密码算法。加密另外一样东西，得到一串**密钥流**（keystream），再把密钥流和数据异或。再用同一串密钥流异或一次就还原了，所以解密和加密是同一个操作。

text.en: **Stream cipher mode** makes the keystream by encrypting the IV, then encrypting the result, and so on. The keystream does not depend on the data, but block 1000's piece of it can only be reached by computing the 999 before it.
text.zh: **流密码模式**先加密 IV，再加密得到的结果，如此反复，生成密钥流。密钥流和数据无关，但第 1000 块对应的那段，只有把前面 999 段都算一遍才拿得到。

text.en: **Counter mode** encrypts the IV plus the block's number instead:
text.zh: **计数器模式**加密的是 IV 加上块的编号：

text.en: Block $i$ depends on nothing but the key, the IV and $i$. To read block 1000, compute $E_K(\mathrm{IV} + 1000)$ and XOR it with $C_{1000}$: one encryption, and no other block touched. To change block 1000, do the same and write it back; nothing else changes.
text.zh: 第 $i$ 块只取决于密钥、IV 和 $i$。要读第 1000 块，算出 $E_K(\mathrm{IV} + 1000)$，和 $C_{1000}$ 异或：一次加密，不碰任何别的块。要改第 1000 块，同样算一次再写回去；别的都不用动。

prompt.en: ECB also lets you decrypt block 1000 on its own. Why is counter mode still the better answer?
prompt.zh: ECB 也能单独解密第 1000 块。为什么答案仍然是计数器模式？

label.en: In ECB identical plaintext blocks give identical ciphertext blocks, which reveals patterns
label.zh: ECB 里相同的明文块得到相同的密文块，会暴露规律

label.en: ECB cannot decrypt a single block
label.zh: ECB 没法单独解密一块

feedback.en: It can: each block is encrypted on its own. The trouble is what that reveals.
feedback.zh: 能：每块都是单独加密的。问题在于这会暴露什么。

feedback.en: Speed is not the issue; both need one block encryption per block.
feedback.zh: 问题不在速度；两者每块都只需要一次分组加密。

explain.en: Counter mode keeps ECB's independence of blocks but, because each block's number goes into the cipher, two identical plaintext blocks come out different.
explain.zh: 计数器模式保留了 ECB 各块独立的好处，但因为每块的编号都进了密码算法，两个相同的明文块加密出来是不一样的。

items.en: **The mechanism**: each block is XORed with $E_K(\mathrm{IV} + i)$, which depends only on the block's position, so any block can be encrypted or decrypted on its own.
items.zh: **机制**：每块和 $E_K(\mathrm{IV} + i)$ 异或，它只取决于这一块的位置，所以任何一块都能单独加密或解密。

items.en: **The contrast**: chained modes (CBC, CFB) make each block depend on the ciphertext before it, so a block in the middle cannot be handled on its own.
items.zh: **对比**：链式模式（CBC、CFB）让每块都依赖它前面的密文，中间的块没法单独处理。

title.zh: 复习课 (1) 第 2 题 · 满分答案

paras.en: Counter mode is best suited. In counter mode the cipher encrypts the initialisation vector plus the block number, and the result is XORed with the plaintext block, so each block can be encrypted or decrypted on its own, based only on its location in the file, without processing any other block. Chained modes such as cipher block chaining or cipher feedback make each block depend on the ciphertext before it (cipher feedback needs the 8 preceding bytes of ciphertext), so accessing a block in the middle requires other parts of the file, and changing one block would change all the blocks after it. (ECB would allow random access but reveals repeated plaintext blocks.)
paras.zh: 计数器模式最合适。计数器模式加密的是初始化向量加上块号，再把结果和明文块异或，所以每一块都能只根据它在文件中的位置单独加密或解密，不需要处理任何别的块。密码块链接、密码反馈这类链式模式让每一块都依赖它前面的密文（密码反馈需要前面 8 个字节的密文），访问中间的一块就得用到文件的其他部分，而且改动一块会让它后面的所有块都跟着变。（ECB 虽然也能随机访问，但会暴露重复的明文块。）

text.en: The lecturer's answer names the contrast with cipher feedback explicitly. Naming one chained mode and why it fails is what turns *counter mode* into an explanation.
text.zh: 老师的答案特意点出了和密码反馈模式的对比。说出一种链式模式以及它为什么不行，才让“计数器模式”成为一个解释。

title.zh: 同一串密钥流绝不能用两次

text.en: Counter mode and stream cipher mode share a weakness the course calls the **keystream reuse attack**. If two messages are encrypted with the same key and the same IV, they are XORed with the same keystream $K_0$. An eavesdropper XORs the two ciphertexts, and the keystream cancels out:
text.zh: 计数器模式和流密码模式有一个共同的弱点，课上叫它**密钥流重用攻击**（keystream reuse attack）。如果两条消息用同一个密钥、同一个 IV 加密，它们就是和同一串密钥流 $K_0$ 异或的。窃听者把两段密文异或，密钥流就抵消了：

text.en: What is left is the XOR of the two plaintexts. Knowing or guessing either one (a standard header, a common word) reveals the other. So the IV must never repeat under the same key: choose keys and IVs independently and at random, and never reuse a counter value. For an encrypted file that is rewritten, that means a fresh IV when the file is re-encrypted.
text.zh: 剩下的是两段明文的异或。知道或猜出其中一段（一个标准文件头、一个常见的词），另一段就暴露了。所以同一个密钥下 IV 绝不能重复：密钥和 IV 要独立、随机地选，计数器的值也绝不能重用。对一个会被重写的加密文件来说，就是重新加密时要换一个新的 IV。

rows.en: A file read and written at random places
rows.zh: 一个在任意位置读写的文件

rows.en: Keystrokes, encrypted as they are typed
works a byte at a time
A noisy link, where one bad bit should not spread
rows.zh: 有噪声的链路，错一位不该扩散

rows.en: a wrong ciphertext bit flips just one plaintext bit
rows.zh: 密文错一位，明文也只错一位

rows.en: Encrypting on many processors at once
rows.zh: 在许多处理器上同时加密
没有哪一块要等别的块
ECB 会把重复暴露出来

text.en: Error spread is a favourite comparison. In CBC a wrong bit in one ciphertext block garbles that whole block and flips one bit in the next; in CFB it spoils 9 bytes; in stream cipher and counter mode it flips only the one matching plaintext bit, because the keystream does not depend on the ciphertext.
text.zh: 错误扩散是考题里常比的一项。CBC 里一个密文块错一位，会把这一整块弄乱，并让下一块错一位；CFB 里会坏掉 9 个字节；流密码和计数器模式里只让对应的那一位明文出错，因为密钥流不依赖密文。

prompt.en: A remote terminal encrypts each keystroke the moment it is typed, one byte at a time. Which mode fits best?
prompt.zh: 一个远程终端在每次击键时立即加密，一次一个字节。哪种模式最合适？

feedback.en: CBC encrypts whole blocks of 16 bytes (AES); it would have to wait for 16 keystrokes before sending anything.
feedback.zh: CBC 加密的是整块（AES 是 16 字节）；它得等攒够 16 次击键才能发出去。

feedback.en: Also block by block, and it would encrypt the same key the same way every time.
feedback.zh: 同样是一整块一整块地来，而且同一个按键每次都加密成同样的东西。

explain.en: CFB works byte by byte, so each keystroke can be encrypted and sent at once. The course's slide names exactly this use.
explain.zh: CFB 一个字节一个字节地处理，每次击键都能马上加密发出。课件举的正是这个用法。

title.en: Your turn: the same key and IV twice
title.zh: 你来：同一个密钥和 IV 用了两次

prompt.en: Two files are encrypted in counter mode with the same key and the same IV. What can an eavesdropper who has both ciphertexts compute, without the key?
prompt.zh: 两个文件用计数器模式、同一个密钥和同一个 IV 加密。拿到两段密文的窃听者，不用密钥能算出什么？

label.en: The XOR of the two plaintexts
Nothing: without the key the ciphertexts are random
label.zh: 什么也算不出：没有密钥，密文就是随机的

feedback.en: Each is random on its own, but they were made with the same keystream, which cancels out when the two are XORed.
feedback.zh: 单看每一段是随机的，但它们用的是同一串密钥流，两段一异或，密钥流就抵消了。

feedback.en: The key stays hidden; what leaks is the relation between the plaintexts, which is often enough.
feedback.zh: 密钥仍然是安全的；泄露的是两段明文之间的关系，而这往往就够了。

explain.en: $(P \oplus K) \oplus (Q \oplus K) = P \oplus Q$. With a guess at either file, the other follows.
explain.zh: $(P \oplus K) \oplus (Q \oplus K) = P \oplus Q$。猜出其中一个文件，另一个就出来了。

title.en: Your turn: one wrong bit in CFB

prompt.en: In cipher feedback mode with an 8-byte register, one bit of the ciphertext is corrupted. How many bytes of the decrypted text are affected?
prompt.zh: 在使用 8 字节寄存器的密码反馈模式里，密文有一位出错。解密后的文本有几个字节受影响？

explain.en: The byte itself, plus the next 8, during which the wrong byte sits in the register: 9.
explain.zh: 它自己那个字节，再加上后面 8 个——在这期间出错的字节一直待在寄存器里：一共 9 个。

prompt.en: ECB mode allows random access too. Explain why it is still a poor choice for encrypting a large image or database file.
prompt.zh: ECB 模式也能随机访问。解释为什么用它来加密一个大的图像或数据库文件仍然不好。

key_points.en: In ECB the same plaintext block always gives the same ciphertext block
key_points.zh: ECB 里同样的明文块总是得到同样的密文块

key_points.en: Large files contain many repeated blocks, so the patterns stay visible to an eavesdropper
key_points.zh: 大文件里有很多重复的块，规律对窃听者仍然可见

key_points.en: An attacker can also swap or replay blocks; counter mode gives random access without this
key_points.zh: 攻击者还能调换或重放块；计数器模式能随机访问却没有这个问题

model_answer.en: In ECB each block is encrypted on its own with the same key, so identical plaintext blocks give identical ciphertext blocks. An image has large areas of the same colour and a database has records with the same fields, so the structure of the data remains visible, and an attacker can swap or replay blocks. Counter mode keeps random access but mixes each block's position into its encryption, so repeated blocks look different.
model_answer.zh: ECB 用同一个密钥单独加密每一块，相同的明文块得到相同的密文块。图像里有大片相同的颜色，数据库里有字段相同的记录，于是数据的结构依然看得出来，攻击者还能调换或重放块。计数器模式保留了随机访问，又把每块的位置混进了它的加密，重复的块看起来就不一样了。

explain.en: Random access is not the only requirement of a good mode: hiding repeats is the reason modes beyond ECB exist.
explain.zh: 随机访问不是好模式的唯一要求：藏住重复，正是 ECB 之外那些模式存在的理由。
